note: Binds GOAL_SPEC.md 9.1 outputs 5 through 9 for the four foundational proof families whose outputs 1 through 4 were measured PASS at issue #481. Outputs 1 through 4 are inherited and are NOT re-claimed here. This artifact records LOCAL_PASS or OPEN per family per output and claims no Q57/QG3 LIVE_PASS. Output 5 was OPEN for all four families at issue #482 because the maximum/adversarial fixture measured that the L1 envelope is EXHAUSTIBLE on the redeemer-carried route: every forced MPF branch level costs a measured 276 complete-signed-transaction bytes, and reaching the level that exhausts the 16,384-byte envelope is a fixed-target search of about 2^(4i) digests. That measurement stands: it is re-run here, its marginal cost is unchanged, and finding Q1X-F5 keeps it. What changed at issue #545 is that the route is no longer the only one. All four families were wired onto published-chunk carriage (midgard/fraud_proofs/chunked_inclusion_v1 delegating to the merkelized mpf_chunked_verify validator over midgard/mpf_chunked_proof_v1), whose step transaction is byte-identical at branch level 22 and at branch level 32 — the depth a 2^128 adversary reaches. The carriage dispatch this adds costs the redeemer-carried route a measured constant of about 700 script bytes, lowering ITS ceiling from branch level 21..23 to 19..20 (2^76 work at the cheapest family); that shift is recorded in adversarialDepthBound.constantShiftNote rather than hidden. Output 5 is re-decided per family: LOCAL_PASS where the chunked route is emulator-measured end to end AND no adversarial axis remains unexercised for that family (Q12, Q14); still OPEN for Q10 and Q11, whose second axis, spend-input preimage cardinality, is unmeasured (finding Q1X-F6).

adversarialDepthBound.measuredTitle: bounds the membership-depth axis with a measured marginal cost per level
adversarialDepthBound.construction: Two siblings are deterministically grinded per level so that the challenged transaction's hashed path branches at every nibble 0..N-1, each into a DISTINCT nibble slot. Distinct slots are what force a three-child node, which is what makes every on-path proof step serialize as MPF's largest `branch` shape rather than the cheaper `fork` or `leaf`. Candidate keys are a counter written into a fixed buffer, so the fixture is byte-for-byte reproducible.
adversarialDepthBound.cborVersusTransactionNote: The 139-byte figure is the MPF library's own compact CBOR cost per branch step, measured separately at levels 1 through 5 with exactly constant differences. The 276-byte figure is the cost in the COMPLETE SIGNED transaction, which is what the L1 envelope measures, and is roughly double because the proof reaches the chain as Plutus data in the step redeemer. Using the smaller number for envelope arithmetic would understate the exposure by a factor of two; both are pinned so that substitution cannot happen silently.
adversarialDepthBound.workModel: Forcing a branch at level i requires a transaction whose hashed path agrees with the challenged transaction's path on i chosen nibbles. That is a fixed-target search, not a birthday search, so it costs about 16^i = 2^(4i) candidate hashings, and the whole ladder is dominated by its last rung.
adversarialDepthBound.constantShiftNote: The per-level cost is unchanged at 276 complete-signed-transaction bytes; what moved between issue #482 and issue #545 is the CONSTANT. Every step that can open a trie now carries the carriage dispatch that lets a prover choose published-chunk carriage, which costs a measured ~700 bytes of spending script and lowers this route's ceiling from branch level 21..23 to 19..20. That is the price of the remediation, and it is paid on the route being remediated: the chunked route it buys has a marginal cost of zero bytes per level and is measured out to level 32 (chunkedProofCarriage). Keeping the walk itself in the merkelized mpf_chunked_verify validator rather than inlining it into every step is what holds the shift to ~700 bytes; inlining measured ~3,700 and took this ceiling to 8..9.

outputStatus.title: Maximum/adversarial proof-fit fixture
outputStatus.evidence: Four measurements now exist. Issue #482 added the first threshold-enforcing measurement of the complete correction path on the MINIMAL fixture; re-run after the #545 wiring its worst byte margins are Q10 5436 at step-02, Q11 5384 at step-01, Q12 5365 at step-01, Q14 5672 at step-01. The #481 residual added the MAXIMUM/adversarial fixture: a deterministically grinded block forcing five all-branch levels into each family's step-01 membership proof, and for Q11 into the step-04 non-membership proof as well, with the marginal cost of one further level measured at two real depths (276 complete-signed-transaction bytes, 48,237 execution memory units, 14,876,759 execution steps) and the resulting envelope ceiling at branch level 19 to 20. Issue #545 added the third: the same real prepare/submit pipeline with the proof carried by published chunks and verified by the merkelized mpf_chunked_verify validator, driven at branch level 22 — past every family's direct-route ceiling — end to end for Q14 (worst byte margin 3339 at step-01) and Q12 (worst byte margin 3049 at step-01). Issue #549 completed that route for the remaining two families, whose openings are of one shared root rather than one apiece: Q10 carries both membership proofs by chunks (worst byte margin 3249 at step-02) and Q11 carries its membership proof and its step-04 ABSENCE proof by chunks (worst byte margin 2790 at step-04), each including every publication, every step and the block removal, every stage inside the 20% execution reserve. Issue #549 also added the fourth: the second adversarial axis, spend-input preimage cardinality, measured through the same pipeline for Q10 and Q11 — and it does not fit.
outputStatus.whyOpen: Q12 and Q14 are LOCAL_PASS: their maximum is measured to FIT, because the depth an adversary can force no longer reaches the step transaction, and neither family carries the second adversarial axis at all (the invalid-range steps operate on the compact transaction and the zero-input family's challenged transaction spends nothing by construction). Q10 and Q11 stay OPEN, and no longer for want of a measurement: their chunked lifecycles are now measured end to end at branch level 22 like their siblings', but the second axis IS measured and DOES NOT FIT. The admissible spend-input cardinality is 296 and the correction paths run out of execution memory at 40 (Q10) and 41 (Q11); at 296 neither proof can be evaluated at all. Finding Q1X-F6 records the numbers, and unlike Q1X-F5 it is not remediable by carriage: the cost is the step's reproduction of an authenticated collection, not the travel of any bytes.

adversarialAxes.note: Enlarging a native transaction's OUTPUTS does not grow these transactions, because the step redeemer carries native_tx_compact_cbor, whose fields are hashes rather than preimages. Only the paths that carry actual preimages grow. Issue #482's expectation that the binding constraint would be the witness PUBLICATION transaction is measured false (spendInputCardinalityBound.expectationCorrected): the publication is under two kilobytes at the boundary, and what binds is the execution memory of re-hashing the authenticated collection inside the step. Unlike the membership-depth axis this is not remediable by moving bytes, so no carriage settles it. See finding Q1X-F6.

residualFindings.finding: Output 5 is closed for Q12 and Q14 and remains OPEN for Q10 and Q11. The maximum/adversarial fixture that #482 recorded as missing exists and is runner-measured, and what it measures — that the redeemer-carried maximum does not fit (Q1X-F5) — is remediated by published-chunk carriage, now measured end to end for all four families (chunkedProofCarriage). Q10 and Q11 stay OPEN on the second axis alone (Q1X-F6), which does not apply to Q12 or Q14, and which is no longer unexercised: it is measured, and it does not fit.

Q10, Q11 and Q12 have no emulator valid-block negative, and Q14's is a step-advance negative rather than a full valid-block finalization negative. True valid-block emulator negatives exist for other families (input-no-idx and da-hash-preimage), so the pattern is available and the omission is a breadth gap, not a structural impossibility.
Q11's emulator journey does not assert slashingApproach, unlike Q10, Q12 and Q14. The removal still executes, but the correct-slashing half of 9.1 output 9 is asserted only indirectly for Q11.

The emulator runs at maxTxSize 65536 while proof fit is judged against the real 16384-byte L1 limit through l1ByteMargin. The two are deliberately different: the relaxed emulator ceiling lets a would-be-oversize transaction be built and then measured rather than failing opaquely during construction. Any future change to EMULATOR_PROTOCOL_PARAMETERS.maxTxSize must not be mistaken for a change in the pass criterion.

REMEDIATED BY CARRIAGE, measurement retained. The 16,384-byte L1 envelope on the REDEEMER-CARRIED step-01 proof transaction is exhaustible by a block producer willing to grind: each forced MPF branch level costs a measured 276 bytes of complete signed transaction, so that route runs out at branch level 20 (Q10), 20 (Q11), 19 (Q12) and 20 (Q14). Forcing level i is a fixed-target search costing about 2^(4i) candidate hashings, so the cheapest of the four is exhaustible at roughly 2^76 work — expensive, but well inside the 2^128 reference adversary, which reaches level 32. Byte fit is the binding envelope: the execution-memory ceiling is 214 levels and the execution-step ceiling 518, both measured. All of that remains true and is still asserted executably by the maximum fixture, which fails if the ceiling ever moves. Those ceilings are two to three levels lower than the 21..23 issue #482 published, because every step that can open a trie now carries the carriage dispatch; the per-level cost is unchanged, only the constant moved, and adversarialDepthBound.constantShiftNote records why. What has changed in substance is that the direct route is no longer the ONLY route: issue #545 wired all four families onto published-chunk carriage, whose step transaction is byte-identical at branch level 22 and at branch level 32 (chunkedProofCarriage.depthInvariance), so the griefing vector no longer censors the correction path. The finding stays recorded rather than deleted because the direct route still ships and a prover who chooses it still faces this ceiling.
residualFindings.owner: remediated at issue #545; the direct-route measurement stays pinned

residualFindings.finding: MEASURED AND DOES NOT FIT. The second adversarial axis, spend-input preimage cardinality, is exercised end to end for Q10 and Q11 at issue #549 and the measurement is a defect rather than a clearance. The admissible cardinality is 296 — the smallest of the consensus profile's 16,384-item guardrail, its 32,768-byte spend-inputs preimage field bound (862 inputs at 38 bytes each), and the Cardano script-spend shape already pinned as maximum_cardano_spend_redeemer_count. Measured against the 20% execution reserve over Cardano's 14,000,000-unit memory cap, Q10's complete correction path fits at 39 inputs (step-04, 11,049,259 memory units) and exceeds the reserve at 40 (11,312,784), and Q11's fits at 40 (step-02, 11,170,542) and exceeds it at 41 (11,465,641). At the admissible 296 neither family's proof can be evaluated at all: both exceed the ledger's own memory cap. So a block producer whose challenged transaction spends 41 admissible inputs censors the Q10 and Q11 correction paths outright, at no grinding cost whatsoever — this axis is free to the adversary, where the membership-depth axis cost about 2^76 digests. The expectation #482 recorded about WHERE it would bind is also measured false: the witness publication transaction is 1,862 bytes at the boundary with 14,522 bytes of margin, and Q11 does not use a witness reference input at all — its step-02 carries the preimage in the step redeemer. Execution memory binds, and published-chunk carriage cannot remediate it, because the cost is the step's reproduction of the whole authenticated collection rather than the travel of any bytes.

chunkedProofCarriage.mechanism: The MPF proof is published beforehand across bounded UTxOs whose inline datum carries nothing but canonical mpf.ProofStep values (mpf_chunked_proof_v1.ProofChunkDatum, at most 16 steps and 2,304 bytes each). The step transaction references them and names their order as indices into tx.reference_inputs; midgard/fraud_proofs/chunked_inclusion_v1 concatenates the chunks and verifies the complete proof atomically against the very root the challenged header commits. The redeemer-carried route is retained unchanged — it is cheaper for every proof that fits — so the carriage is a prover-chosen sum type (NativeTxInclusionCarriage / NonMembershipCarriage), not a replacement.

onchainSeam.whyMerkelized: Compiling the proof walk into every step that can open a trie added a measured ~3,700 bytes to each step's spending script, which the step transaction carries on EITHER route — taking the redeemer-carried route's ceiling from branch level 21..23 down to 8..9. Remediating one route by degrading the other is not a remediation, so the walk lives in one merkelized withdraw validator shared by every family, exactly as phas.ak and pexcludes.ak already host the single-transaction walks. The residual cost to the direct route is the carriage dispatch alone: ~700 bytes, two to three forced levels.

depthInvariance.note: Ten further forced branch levels. On the redeemer-carried route those levels cost 10 * 276 = 2,760 more complete-signed-transaction bytes, which is what exhausts the envelope. Here the step transaction is byte-identical, because it carries one small integer and one reference input per CHUNK rather than per level. The proof itself did grow (3,060 to 4,450 CBOR bytes); only its carriage did not. The depth a 2^128 adversary reaches (32) is therefore no longer a censorship lever on the step transaction.

chunkedProofCarriage.depthConstruction: The depth is synthesised rather than grinded, and deliberately so: a genuinely grinded level-22 trie costs about 2^88 digests, which is the adversary's cost and the whole point of finding Q1X-F5, not something a fixture can pay. The proof is a real MPF proof of a real trie shape (an all-branch ladder, MPF's widest step), verified by the library's own verify, and the challenged header is then made to commit exactly the root that proof proves — so the step's counted-root authentication is genuine. The grinded fixture in submit-init-emulator-max-proof-fit.test.ts remains the source of the COST bound; this one measures carriage. See demo/midgard-fault-proofs/tests/support/synthetic-deep-proof-v1.ts.
chunkedProofCarriage.sharedRootOpenings: Q12 and Q14 open the challenged block's transactions trie exactly once, so issue #545 could give each a standalone synthetic ladder. Q10 and Q11 cannot: double-spend opens the SAME root twice for membership (tx1 at step-01, tx2 at step-02) and no-input opens it once for membership and once for ABSENCE (the phantom input's producing transaction, at step-04), and every step re-authenticates its opening against the one root the challenged header commits. Two independent ladders each determine their own root, so the fixture builds what a real trie would hold instead: one shared branch node whose child slots carry the sub-tries of the individual ladders, with every opening's top-level neighbours read out of that same node. The library's own Proof.verify is what confirms each opening reconstructs the one root. See syntheticDeepSharedRootProofsV1 in demo/midgard-fault-proofs/tests/support/synthetic-deep-proof-v1.ts.
chunkedProofCarriage.secondPublicationNote: Q10 and Q11 publish twice, because each opens the trie twice and a publication carries one proof. The second publication is submitted immediately before the step that consumes it, which is also what keeps its UTxOs out of every earlier transaction's fee selection. Both publications survive the steps that reference them, which the suite asserts.
chunkedProofCarriage.executionUnitsNote: Every stage of every journey is asserted against the 20% execution reserve by the runner-executed helper; the numbers recorded here are the proof-carrying stages of one measured run. They drift in the last digits run to run because the emulator-derived validity interval moves, so the threshold assertion is the binding claim, not these constants.

spendInputCardinalityBound.derivationTitle: derives the admissible spend-input cardinality from the consensus profile
spendInputCardinalityBound.admissibilityDerivation: Three protocol constraints bound how many inputs an admissible challenged transaction may spend, and the smallest is the one a fraud proof must survive. (1) MIDGARD_CONSENSUS_LIMITS_V1.maxSpendInputCount = 16,384, which is bounded_collection_v1.max_tx_size_derived_item_count in onchain/aiken/lib/midgard/bounded-collection-v1.ak; its own source calls it a one-byte-per-item encoding floor that can never reject a shape Cardano could fit, so it is a guardrail, not the effective bound. (2) MIDGARD_CONSENSUS_LIMITS_V1.maxSpendInputsPreimageBytes = 32,768, twice the preserved L1 envelope, in demo/midgard-core/src/consensus-profile-v1.ts; at 38 bytes per canonical TransactionInput item it admits 862. (3) The Cardano script-spend shape boundary this repository already pins: 296 inputs each carrying a spend redeemer, maximum_cardano_spend_redeemer_count in onchain/aiken/lib/midgard/fraud-proofs/native-tx.max-redeemers.test.ak, which validators/fraud-proofs/input-no-idx/step-02.ak already names as the shape a Q13 proof must handle. 296 is the smallest, and is the admissible cardinality these two families are measured against.
spendInputCardinalityBound.ceilingNote: The boundary is measured against Cardano's own 14,000,000-unit transaction memory cap, which is what EMULATOR_PROTOCOL_PARAMETERS carries and what every other execution measurement in this artifact is judged by. That cap is BELOW the consensus profile's 16,500,000-unit capability floor, so the measured cardinality ceiling is the conservative one; raising the ceiling to the profile floor moves it by single digits, not by the two orders of magnitude the admissible shape is away.
spendInputCardinalityBound.expectationCorrected: Issue #482 recorded an expectation that this axis would bind on the spend-inputs WITNESS PUBLICATION transaction and on execution units rather than on the step transaction's own bytes. Half of that is now measured false. The publication transaction is not the constraint at all: at Q10's boundary it is 1,862 bytes with 14,522 bytes of margin, and the steps that reference it are within five bytes of their minimal-fixture size, exactly because the preimage is a reference input's datum. And Q11 is not shaped that way in the first place: no-input step-02 carries inputs_preimage in the STEP REDEEMER (midgard/fraud_proofs/no_input/step_02.Args), so the axis does reach that transaction's bytes there, and still does not bind, with 10,684 bytes of margin at the boundary. Execution memory binds, in both families, because a step must re-hash the whole authenticated bounded collection before it may select one item from it.
spendInputCardinalityBound.buildsAtAdmissibleCardinalityTitle: cannot build either family's proof at the admissible Cardano spend shape
spendInputCardinalityBound.whyNotRemediableByCarriage: Published-chunk carriage remediated Q1X-F5 by moving the proof's BYTES out of the step transaction. There is nothing to move here: the cost is the step's own re-hashing of a bounded collection it must reproduce in full before it may select one item from it, and that work is the same wherever the preimage travelled from. A remediation would have to change what the step proves — an item-level proof against the collection commitment rather than a whole-collection reproduction, which bounded_collection_v1.verify_item already supports and no foundational family's step uses.
